subject: Private deployment connectivity strategy: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN (request)
messages:
From: Lucia Santos <lucia@medibridge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 08:53:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — need recommendation

Hi Rishi / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the intro last week. We're starting a proof-of-concept to host sensitive inference workloads in a private deployment and need guidance on the networking approach. High-level constraints:
- Data classification: PCI + PHI in scope, must stay within our VPCs and on-premise systems.
- Latency: 10ms p99 for critical inference path preferred for our US-east region.
- Throughput: ~200 req/s spikes to 1k for batch periods.
- Multi-region: production will have east & west regions; prefer a single model endpoint type for both if possible.
- Audit/controls: need mutual TLS, flow logs, and evidentiary logs for SOC2 audit.

We heard VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) and site-to-site IPsec VPN are the common choices. Could you assemble a short recommendation that weighs operational complexity, security posture, latency tradeoffs, and our ability to meet audit requirements? Also include a simple rollout approach (pilot -> canary -> scale) and any ask lists for our networking team.

Attached is a small topology sketch and our expected QPS distribution.

Appreciate a concise set of options we can present to our infra/security folks.

Regards,
Lucia Santos
Dir, Platform Engineering
MediBridge Health

Attachments: topology-sketch.png (image), initial-qps-profile.csv (csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Santos <lucia@medibridge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — need recommendation

Lucia — thanks, this is a clear brief. High-level — we can support all three patterns but they map differently to your constraints.

Summary up front (short):
- PrivateLink: best for strong isolation and least blast radius; interface endpoints per region; additional effort for cross-account endpoint management; predictable security posture for SOC2. Latency: typically low but depends on AZ topology.
- VPC Peering: lowest hop-count (good latency), simple routing; becomes complex at scale (mesh complexity, overlapping CIDRs) and cross-account peering has more governance work. Good for high-throughput, low-latency within same cloud provider/region.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec): easiest for rapid proof-of-concept and on-prem integration; typically higher latency and less stable for p99 SLAs unless you use managed HA appliances or AWS Transit Gateway + VPN with BGP; also brings broader network surface to your DC.

I'll pull together a short decision matrix and an ask checklist for your network/security teams. Can you confirm: are you planning to run Redwood Private in your AWS accounts (customer-managed VPCs) or expect Redwood-managed VPC endpoints (cross-account)? Also confirm whether you have a strict non-overlapping CIDR policy; that will affect peering feasibility.

I'll attach a minimal data collection CSV for the items we need (subnet/CIDR info, preferred regions, egress constraints, required port lists).

Best,
Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Rishi / Lucia — adding some pragmatic tradeoffs we use internally when advising customers. I'm keeping this short so you can use it in your architecture review: 

Tradeoff bullets (practical):
- Security & compliance: PrivateLink gives tightest control — Redwood's private endpoints reduce need for broad routing changes and simplify egress audit (interface endpoints + VPC endpoint policies). For SOC2 evidence, we recommend endpoint-level logging + flow logs exported to your secure S3.
- Latency: VPC Peering wins in same-region inter-VPC traffic (single hop). If you need <10ms p99, verify cross-AZ routing paths; in some clouds PrivateLink traffic traverses additional hops to the NLB/endpoint.
- Operational scale: For multi-account large orgs, peering is brittle (N^2 peering problem). We prefer PrivateLink or Transit Gateway patterns for scale; Transit Gateway can centralize but is an extra managed component (cost + ops).
- On-prem access: If you have legacy on-prem apps that must call the endpoint, VPN or Direct Connect + PrivateLink dual-path is common: e.g., Direct Connect into a hub VPC that hosts the PrivateLink endpoints.

Recommended pilot approach for MediBridge (concise):
1) Pilot in us-east-1 with PrivateLink (single AZ endpoint per AZ) to validate IAM endpoint policies and audit logging.
2) Run latency tests vs peered VPC (temp peering) to confirm p99 target. If peering consistently wins by margin and you can accept the CIDR/scale tradeoffs, consider peering in region only.
3) For on-prem connectivity, prototype an IPsec tunnel to the hub VPC; use it as a fallback and for admin tooling, not production inference traffic unless SLA proven.

Operational asks for your networking team (checklist):
- Confirm CIDR blocks and any overlapping ranges.
- Identify the account where endpoints will live (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
- Provide required egress IP ranges for firewall allowlisting.
- Approve CloudWatch/VPC Flow Log sink and S3 bucket ARN for audit exports.

I'll assemble a one-page decision matrix and a short runbook (pilot steps) and mark sections for your network/security approvals. Attaching our reference brief.

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-privatedeploy-reference.pdf (stub)
